body: Water moves among the ocean, atmosphere, soil, organisms, rivers, lakes and ice. Evaporation transfers water from a liquid surface to water vapor. Cooling can produce droplets or ice in clouds. Precipitation can return water to the surface, where some runs into rivers or seeps into the ground.

Near standard atmospheric pressure of 101,325 pascals, pure water freezes near 273 kelvin and boils near 373 kelvin. Changing pressure changes the temperature at which it boils. Dissolved material can also shift freezing and boiling behavior. These are examples of how the same substance changes form.
credit: Centauri Archive editorial draft, written with AI assistance
limitations: The rounded temperatures describe pure water near equilibrium. A picture of a cloud shows droplets or ice rather than gaseous water vapor.
purpose: Trace water movement and changing states across terrestrial reservoirs.
